slot.brief: count arrangements/selections with at least one condition satisfied using total minus the complementary count

stem: How many different arrangements of the letters of the word DELHI have at least one vowel in an odd position?

verdicts.working: Total arrangements = 5! = 120. If neither vowel is in an odd position, E and I occupy the two even positions in 2! ways, and the consonants fill the remaining positions in 3! ways: 12. Thus 120 − 12 = 108.

working:
Total arrangements of the 5 distinct letters = 5! = 120.
Complement: no vowel (E, I) in an odd position (positions 1, 3, 5). Since there are only 2 even positions (2, 4) and 2 vowels, both vowels must occupy the even positions. Number of ways = 2! (arrangements of vowels) × 3! (arrangements of consonants D, L, H in odd positions) = 2 × 6 = 12.
Arrangements with at least one vowel in an odd position = 120 – 12 = 108.

Independent check: Total arrangements = 5! = 120. If neither vowel is in an odd position, E and I occupy the two even positions in 2! ways, and the consonants fill the remaining positions in 3! ways: 12. Thus 120 − 12 = 108.
solution:
There are $5!$ total arrangements. The complement has neither vowel in an odd position, so $E$ and $I$ must occupy positions $2$ and $4$.
$$5!-(2!)(3!)=120-12=108$$
